title: Sound and Water Waves
seo_title: Grade 6 Science: Sound and Water Waves Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_code: Grade 6, Quarter 3: Force, Motion, and Energy
standard_text: Waves carry energy. Water waves are transverse waves; sound waves are longitudinal waves made by vibrations and need a medium. Waves have amplitude, wavelength and frequency; the pitch and loudness of sound depend on frequency and amplitude. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 6, Quarter 3: Force, Motion, and Energy)
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 3: Force, Motion, and Energy): vibrations, how sound travels, pitch and loudness, echoes, and transverse and longitudinal waves. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Sound is a longitudinal wave; water waves are transverse.
body_html:
How to think about it

A wave carries energy from one place to another. In a transverse wave, such as a water wave, the particles move up and down while the wave moves forward. In a longitudinal wave, such as sound, the particles move back and forth in the same direction as the wave.

Sound is made by vibrations and needs a medium (solid, liquid or gas). A higher frequency gives a higher pitch; a bigger amplitude gives a louder sound. Sound reflects off walls as an echo.

Example

Is sound transverse or longitudinal?

Particles move back and forth.

Answer: longitudinal

Example

A guitar string vibrates faster. What happens to the pitch?

Frequency

Answer: it gets higher

Common mistakes

  • Thinking water moves along with the wave.
  • Mixing up pitch and loudness.
  • Thinking sound travels in space.
